lessons.title: Lesson 1: Setup Sprint, Open Every Door
lessons.goal: Reagan creates the starting workspace first: Claude access, Codex access, Telegram installed, and a proof folder ready before the concepts get heavy.
sections: Why this comes first
This course starts with a real setup win. Before learning all the terms, open the tools, create the proof folder, and make sure you can come back tomorrow without starting over.
Create the AI Workspace folder
Create a folder named AI Workspace. Inside it, make a Proof folder and a Notes folder. This is where screenshots, Markdown files, and progress exports will live.
Open the tools
Create or log into Claude. Create or log into Codex with the account CJ provides. Install Telegram if needed. Do not save or screenshot passwords, tokens, or private client data.
Start the proof log
Create proof-log.md. Add today’s date, the tool names, and one line for each status: Claude open, Codex open, Telegram installed, Drive folder created.
Submit
Submit one screenshot of the AI Workspace folder and one screenshot showing each tool is reachable. Hide private values. If a login needs CJ, write waiting on CJ next to that item.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Claude Setup and First Useful Prompt

video.title: Getting started with Claude.ai
video.purpose: Set up Claude, log in, and understand the first clicks without a long tutorial.

lessons.goal: Reagan confirms Claude access and learns how to ask for useful help without pasting private information.
sections: Warm up
Claude is the thinking partner. Use it for writing, planning, summarizing, and explaining. It is not a password vault and it does not replace judgment.
Watch with purpose
Watch the 5:19 Anthropic video. Pause after the first prompt example and write what made the prompt clear.
Build
Ask Claude to create a 5 step plan for setting up your AI workspace for this course. Then ask it to make the plan shorter and more direct.
Save
Paste the final plan into prompts.md and write one sentence about what made the second version better.
Submit
Submit a screenshot showing Claude open and paste the final 5 step plan into your workbook.

sections: Warm up
Codex is for building, editing, reviewing, and checking work. Think of it as another smart teammate, not a magic button.
Setup
Create or log into the account CJ provides. Confirm you can open Codex and start a task. Keep private data out of test prompts.
Watch with purpose
Watch the OpenAI video. Write one thing Codex does that feels different from a normal chat.
Build
Give Codex a simple sample task: review this checklist for clarity. Use fake content, not private CJ business data.
Submit
Submit a screenshot showing Codex access and 3 bullets on when you would choose Codex instead of Claude.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Set Up Your Telegram Agent

sections: Warm up
Telegram is the front door. The agent is the worker behind it. BotFather creates the bot account, then Hermes connects the bot to the agent.
Watch with purpose
Watch the 1:34 BotFather clip. Write down what BotFather creates and what it does not create.
Setup
Create the Telegram bot with BotFather. Save the bot name. Do not paste the bot token into public docs or screenshots. CJ approves the token connection step.
Hermes connection
Follow the guided internal setup for the Telegram gateway. Confirm you can send one message to the bot and get one response back.
Proof
Submit a screenshot of the bot chat working, with any private token hidden. Add the bot name and the date to proof-log.md.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: LLMs, Agents, Skills, Commands, Tools, and MCPs

video.title: What are AI agents? AI Agents Explained in 2 minutes
video.purpose: Quick visual intro to agents before CJ examples.

lessons.goal: Reagan can explain the core agent language in plain English and connect each word to the setup she just built.
sections: Start from what you built
Look at your setup proof. Claude is an LLM. Hermes through Telegram is an agent front door. Codex is a build focused AI teammate. The terms make more sense after the tools are open.
LLM vs agent
An LLM thinks and answers. An agent thinks and acts with tools, memory, rules, and a goal. Simple line: chatbot answers, agent gets work done.
Watch with purpose
Watch the 2 minute agent clip. Write down the first moment where the video moves from talking to doing.
Building blocks
A command tells the agent what to do. A skill is a saved best practice. A tool lets the agent touch the outside world. An MCP is a clean way to connect tools and data.
Build
Add a glossary to my-ai-workspace.md with: LLM, agent, command, skill, tool, MCP, wiki, vault, closeout, Drive backup. Use your own words.

quiz.q: What is the cleanest difference between an LLM and an agent?
choices: An LLM answers, an agent can act with tools
They are the exact same thing

quiz.q: What is a skill in this course?
choices: A saved best practice the agent can reuse

quiz.q: What is an MCP?
choices: A standard connection that lets an agent use outside tools or data

quiz.q: Which example fits an agent best?
choices: Search Drive, find a file, update a project, and report proof

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Markdown, Saved Work, Drive Backup, and Closeout

video.title: Markdown in 2 Minutes
video.purpose: Show Markdown as simple structured text before she builds workspace files.

lessons.goal: Reagan builds the habit of saving useful work in Markdown, backing it up, and closing the loop with proof.
sections: Markdown is the playbook
Markdown is plain text with structure. Use headings, bullets, links, screenshots, and checklists. It keeps work readable for people and useful for agents.
Karpathy style setup
Start every workspace with clear context, examples, constraints, and proof. The agent should not guess where things live or what good looks like.
Drive backup
Local files are not enough. Back up the AI Workspace folder to Google Drive so Rea can recover progress and CJ can review proof fast.
Closeout habit
Every session ends with what changed, where it lives, proof, and the next step. If it is not written down, it did not happen.
Build
Create or update my-ai-workspace.md, prompts.md, proof-log.md, and closeout.md. Add today’s setup notes and one clean next step.

lessons.title: Lesson 7: First Project, My AI Workspace

video.title: How To Use Google Drive
video.purpose: Show the backup habit for files, screenshots, and proof.

lessons.goal: Reagan finishes with a real AI workspace, saved progress, a Drive backup, and a clear resume point.
sections: Project brief
Build My AI Workspace. It should prove she can log into Claude, use Codex, message the Telegram agent, explain the agent language, save Markdown notes, and back up proof.
Progress save
Use the Save progress button in this course. Download the progress file. Upload it to the AI Workspace folder in Google Drive.
Drive backup
Back up my-ai-workspace.md, prompts.md, proof-log.md, closeout.md, the glossary, and screenshots to Drive. The rule is simple: local work plus cloud proof.
Closeout
Write one closeout note: what was set up, what worked, what is still missing, where the files live, and what the next step is.
Submit
Submit the Drive folder link or screenshot, the downloaded progress file, and the final closeout note.

qualityRules: Lesson 1 must start with setup and proof before heavy concepts.
Every lesson must have at least one relevant visual aid: video, graphic, docs card, internal walkthrough, or useful combination.
Quiz correct answers must be varied. Do not make every correct answer A.
Prefer short YouTube clips over generic link cards when a credible short clip exists.
Do not teach tools or frameworks we do not use in CJ operations.
Every setup lesson must include a save, backup, and resume habit.
